short: Closed-loop word synthesis (M06) from a chronic ECoG implant in ALS (M13) holds on six keywords at 80% listener accuracy; standard designs, one participant, stability untested.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06: closed loop, each word decoded with look-ahead and played after it ends) and the setting (M13: chronic ECoG in a speaker with ALS, 5.5 months after training). Both are standard: 2 of 11 prior intracranial synthesis decoders already played audio back in closed loop [@guenther2009; @angrick2021], with one EEG loop besides [@brumberg2018], and one participant with pooled sessions gives no repetition. The main claim holds narrowly: six keywords were identified at 80% against 16.7% chance, the earliest intelligible closed-loop neural synthesis in the prior set; the authors chose delayed word-level feedback deliberately, so it does not test real-time synthesis. The stability claim has no pre-gap comparison, as the authors' own call for longer testing concedes, and synthesized words remain far less intelligible than the participant's own speech (99.8%).
